name: PSL tier: Chadlite

card.summary: Chadlite is the PSL tier just below Chad, a benchmark of very high facial attractiveness that members use to set goals for how far looksmaxxing can take them.
card.note: A community rating framework, not a scientific measure; it can feed appearance anxiety.

quick.overview:
Chadlite is one of the tiers of the PSL (Perceived Sexual Levels) scale used on looksmaxxing forums. It sits just below Chad and above high-tier normie, and describes a man seen as strikingly good-looking.

The tier works as a target. Members compare their features to the tier, ask whether a given face will reach it after growth or after procedures, and use it to decide which improvements to pursue, such as eyebrows, skin, jaw or body.
quick.how: On looksmax.org, users post photos or descriptions and ask for a rating, sometimes with qualifiers such as low, mid or high within a tier. Discussion focuses on features like eye area, jaw, maxilla and facial harmony, and on fixable items such as brows and angles.
quick.risks: The scale is an informal peer rating and not a validated measure. Critics quoted in media describe it as pseudoscientific, tied to incel ideology and potentially harmful to mental health, and a tier label can become a source of distress.

lead: Chadlite is a tier in the PSL scale, the rating ladder used in looksmaxxing communities to place male faces from "subhuman" up to "giga Chad". The usual sequence runs subhuman (sub-3), low-tier normie, mid-tier normie, high-tier normie (HTN), Chadlite, Chad and giga Chad [7]. Chadlite is the step directly below Chad and is used for a man whose looks stand out clearly from the average but who is not placed in the top category [7][1].

Looksmaxxers use the tier as a concrete goal. A member who is rated, or who rates himself, as high-tier normie can ask which features separate him from Chadlite, such as eye area, jawline, skin or brows, and then choose softmaxxing steps (grooming, skin care, body fat, photo angle) or hardmaxxing steps (procedures) aimed at those features [3][4]. In this way a label that sounds like a verdict is used as a to-do list for appearance.

The scale is a community convention rather than a published instrument. Descriptions of how many points Chadlite spans differ between sources, and critics, including academic researchers, describe the PSL framework as pseudoscientific and tied to incel ideology [7][8][9]. Research on facial attractiveness generally studies averageness, symmetry and sexual dimorphism in rated faces, and has not tested the PSL tiers themselves [13].

angle.text: The tier gives people a concrete goal for facial improvement. Members use rating feedback to decide what to change, such as eyebrow shape, skin, leanness or camera angle, and then report back with new photos.

infobox: About 6.0 to 6.8 on the 8-point PSL scale[10]

paras: PSL is usually expanded as "Perceived Sexual Levels" and is described as rating facial attractiveness on roughly a 1 to 8 range that is supposed to reflect how women perceive men [7]. The name is commonly traced to three forums, PUAHate, Sluthate and Lookism.net, which Wikipedia calls the PSL forums [7][8]. Know Your Meme records an alternative backronym, "Proportion, Size and Lineation", and describes the scale as presenting geometric and structural criteria such as proportion, bone prominence and contour sharpness as an objective measure [10].

Chadlite is the sixth of the seven named male tiers [7]. A GQ explainer relayed by The Nightly says rankings consider how well features work together, how distinct a face looks from the opposite sex, how sharp the features are and the features themselves, with each tier scored out of 8 according to the population percentile it represents and the remaining points of a 10-point rating coming from sexual market value [11]. Know Your Meme lists a score band for Chadlite and Stacylite of roughly 6.0 to 6.8, glossing it as "attractive by societal standards", with Chad at about 6.9 to 7.4 [10]. Other sites give different numbers; Grokipedia, for example, places Chadlite near 5.5 to 6.5 out of 8 and, separately, describes a 7 out of 10 version used by the YouTuber Wheat Waffles [1]. The differing figures show that the bands are community convention rather than fixed standards.

The female counterpart is Stacylite, within a ladder that runs from Becky (normie tiers) to Stacy (Chad tiers) [10]. Wikipedia's article on incels notes that Chad and Stacy are incel-forum terms for attractive, sexually active men and women, with variants for other groups [12].

sections.h: What Chadlite is said to look like
paras: Descriptions of the tier emphasise facial harmony, a defined jawline with a low gonial angle, a developed maxilla, "hunter eyes" (almond shape, positive canthal tilt, little upper-eyelid exposure) and the absence of obvious asymmetries or flaws such as a dominant nose or poor skin [1][7]. Wikipedia lists hunter eyes, hollow cheeks, a defined jawline and pursed lips among features that looksmaxxers check [7].

Forum rating threads put this in practice. One poster asking about a friend lists an unusually good eye area with a changing grey, blue or turquoise colour, a developed maxilla, a slightly recessed mandible and little under-eye support, and asks whether these will smooth out with age [3]. Another thread has a poster rated "low" or "mid" high-tier normie from front and side photos, with replies saying the profile looks better than the front and suggesting eyebrow work and a better angle [4]. Qualifiers such as low, mid and high within a tier are common, and members dispute the percentile the tier represents, with one thread titled as arguing that Chadlite is not the 97th percentile [2].

Wikipedia dates the PSL scale to 2010s incel and manosphere forums, where men labelled Chads were credited with sexual success, and says looksmaxxing spread to TikTok in the 2020s, mainly through male creators [7]. A 2024 GNET insight by Portsmouth doctoral researcher Anda Solea reported that hashtags tied to the PSL scale and looksmaxxing, such as pslgods and mogging, were trending on TikTok, and that creators used the term Sub5 as a way of reaching audiences without the stigmatised word incel [9].

Media coverage reached a wide audience from 2023: Vice on hunter eyes in June 2023, Business Insider and the New York Times in November 2023, The Conversation in January 2024, The Guardian in February 2024 and the BBC in March 2024, according to Wikipedia's list [7]. In 2026 the New York Times, The Guardian, GQ and The New Yorker covered the streamer Clavicular (Braden Peters), the figure most associated with extreme looksmaxxing [7]. The Nightly, summarising GQ, said he popularised the vocabulary without coining it [11]. Know Your Meme logged a PSL scale entry in February 2026 and credits Clavicular with a role in its spread, citing short-form edits from creators that show PSL scores and before-and-after ascensions [10]. A YouTuber, Wheat Waffles, is credited in Grokipedia with a decile-based rating system that uses Chadlite as a 7 out of 10 tier [1]; that account is unverified elsewhere.

Chadlite appears in thread titles as a rating request ("Chadlite? rate"), a potential question ("chadlite potential?"), and a milestone people ask about when considering procedures [3][4][6]. Members also use it to discuss dating, for example threads asking whether women approach men at Chadlite and above, or remarking on couples where a man rated as Chad is with a woman rated as mid-tier [5][14].

The term also appears as a descriptor for people in videos and news, such as threads about a person who "goes viral on TikTok for no reason" or whose face is said to mog another user's, where Chadlite functions as shorthand for a very good-looking man [15][16]. Members also use the word as a goal in skin, brow and body-fat advice, treating the tier as reachable through changes to modifiable features.

No published study has tested the PSL tiers or Chadlite as a category. Research on facial attractiveness covers related ground: computer face-averaging work such as Murphy and colleagues in 2003, studies of symmetry such as Feng in 2002, and work on sexual dimorphism and cross-cultural agreement, including Cunningham and colleagues in 1995, whose panels of East Asian, Hispanic and White judges agreed on much of what makes a female face attractive [13]. Wikipedia's summary of this literature also records mixed findings, for example that male facial masculinity did not predict attractiveness for female judges in one genetics study [13].

Researchers who have studied the PSL scale are critical. Anda Solea and Lisa Sugiura describe it as a pseudoscientific framework that ranks people by race and gender and argue that incel ideas are being mainstreamed through looksmaxxing language [9][10]. Wikipedia reports that doctors and researchers regard much of the jargon as lacking medical support, and that sociologists such as Halpin and colleagues (2025, Sociology of Health & Illness) analyse the community as promoting a masculine gaze [7]. Psychology Today commentators Heather Widdows and Jessica Sutherland describe male beauty ideals as increasingly demanding, note that boys and men have few spaces to discuss body image, and say forums may offer peer support while calling the trend concerning given its roots [17].

Critics quoted in media link the scale to appearance anxiety and to the movement's origins. Charlie Sabgir, director of the Young Men Research Project, told Rolling Stone that Clavicular's advice normalised self-punishment and that the idea appearance determines outcomes can feed confusion and alienation among young men, as relayed by The Nightly [11]. The New Yorker's Becca Rothfeld described the moral objections to the community, including its "subhuman" label, as numerous, per Wikipedia [7].

Practitioners point to different effects: Wikipedia notes some men report dating success and peer praise, while the same coverage describes praise mixed with critique that keeps lower-rated members in a subordinate position [7].
No studies found. Related research on facial attractiveness judgments exists, but no trial has examined the PSL tiers or whether moving between them changes social or dating outcomes [13].

timeline.event: PSL scale is developed on PUAHate, Sluthate and Lookism.net, according to Wikipedia.[7]

lore.intro: Rating threads treat Chadlite as a benchmark for high attractiveness and a milestone to aim at [3][4].

claims.claim: Chadlite is a distinct, definable attractiveness tier
claims.believers: Members post descriptions and photos asking whether a face qualifies and argue over what percentile it represents [3][4][2].
claims.experts: Critics say the PSL framework is pseudoscientific, and the point values for the tier differ between community sources [9][10].

claims.claim: Facial harmony, dimorphism and a strong eye area are what raise a face to the tier
claims.believers: Rating replies cite eye area, maxilla, mandible and under-eye support as deciding features [3][4].
claims.experts: Attractiveness research studies averageness, symmetry and sexual dimorphism, with mixed results on how masculine faces are judged [13].

claims.claim: Fixable details such as brows and angles can move someone up a tier
claims.believers: A rater tells a poster to fix his eyebrows and use a better angle to improve his rating [4].
claims.experts: No published study has tested whether such changes move a person between PSL tiers.

claims.claim: A higher tier translates into more dating success
claims.believers: Threads ask whether women approach Chadlites and above, and discuss couples in terms of tiers [5][14].
claims.experts: Wikipedia notes that men in the community report mixed experiences of dating and peer praise; the PSL link to outcomes has not been studied [7].

claims.believers: Know Your Meme describes the scale as presented through geometric criteria such as proportion and contour sharpness [10].
claims.experts: Researchers Solea and Sugiura call the framework pseudoscientific, and commentators note that ratings vary with the rater and the photo [9][10].

claims.claim: Face growth after puberty will smooth out features and move someone up
claims.believers: One poster asks whether a friend's slightly recessed mandible will smooth out after age 18 [3].
claims.experts: No published study has tracked PSL tier change over development.
